# LAW 1 — CHARACTER DRAWING

## CORE
`IDENTITY GEOMETRY = CHARACTER-SPECIFIC`
`DRAWING DISCIPLINE = GLOBAL`

Do not standardize anatomy/face/body/hair/silhouette to achieve common style.

Production order:
`BIG SHAPE -> SILHOUETTE -> PRIMARY CONTOUR -> STRUCTURAL INTERNAL LINES -> 4–6 CONTROLLED TONE BANDS -> SPARSE ACCENT DARKS/HIGHLIGHTS -> STOP`

## MEASURED ANCHOR FACTS
Three repeated head components:
- 398x683
- 395x684
- 398x684

Repeat spread:
- width ≈ 0.76%
- height ≈ 0.15%
- foreground area ≈ 1.15%

Foreground luminance:
- mean ≈ 0.293
- p05 ≈ 0.193
- p95 ≈ 0.324

8-cluster palette analysis:
- ≈93.7% foreground = five close mid-tone brown clusters
- ≈3.1% = deepest ink/dark line cluster
- ≈2.0% = deep shadow
- ≈1.2% = light/highlight accents

Line hierarchy on ~397 px head width:
- routine ≈2 px (~0.5% head width)
- strong ≈4 px (~1.0%)
- rare heavy emphasis ≈8–9 px (~2.0–2.3%)

Strong-edge density ≈10.9% foreground at reference model-sheet scale.

## CHARACTER QC ENVELOPE
- dominant large-region palette roughly 4–6 tone bands
- strong-edge density target roughly 8–14% at comparable model-sheet scale
- deep ink sparse by default, usually <5% of skin/face foreground unless Character Truth requires black regions
- no pores / photo noise / random micro-wrinkles
- no continuous glossy 3D shading
- line-weight hierarchy required
- identity geometry drift = FAIL

# LAW 2 — UNIVERSAL TEXTURE / SURFACE

## CORE
`TEXTURE != NOISE`

Every material is:
`BASE FIELD + MACRO FORM + STRUCTURAL EDGES + LIMITED MESO VARIATION + SPARSE MICRO ACCENTS + LIGHT`

Frequency law:
`MACRO > MESO > MICRO`

## MEASURED ANCHOR FACTS
Broad mean luminance:
- far sky/mountains ≈0.420
- mid architecture ≈0.330
- middle ground floor ≈0.311
- foreground floor ≈0.286

Strong-edge density:
- mid architecture ≈10.9%
- middle ground floor ≈6.3%
- foreground floor ≈5.4%

Floor calm-area measurement:
- ≈91.1% below low-gradient threshold (Sobel magnitude <20 on 8-bit luminance)

Inside calm floor zones:
- median fine residual at Gaussian sigma 8 ≈0.20% luminance
- p90 fine residual ≈1.03% luminance

Ground palette compression:
- ≈94–95% of ground band covered by 4–5 close neutral/brown-gray clusters

Coarse/fine residual energy:
- middle ground E16/E1 ≈2.5
- foreground ground E16/E1 ≈3.4

## UNIVERSAL TEXTURE QC ENVELOPE
At intended screen scale, default ordinary production surface:
- calm area usually >=85%
- structural/detail edge coverage usually <=10%
- main material palette roughly 4–6 value/color bands
- coarse-to-fine energy E16/E1 preferably >=2 for calm materials
- fine residual p90 in calm zones preferably <=2% luminance
- random uniform grain = FAIL
- photo texture pasted over simplified geometry = FAIL
- cracks/scratches/grain unrelated to material structure = FAIL
- distance-invariant microdetail = FAIL
- background texture competing with Tier 1 silhouettes = FAIL

Distance law:
- NEAR = macro + meso + sparse selected micro
- MID = macro + meso, micro collapses
- FAR = silhouette + large value/color masses

## RESEARCH BASIS
The laws were checked against established NPR research:
- Gooch et al., SIGGRAPH 1998, `A Non-Photorealistic Lighting Model for Automatic Technical Illustration`: reserve extreme lights/darks for edges/highlights and carry form mainly through mid-tones.
- Lake, Marshall, Harris, Blackstein, NPAR 2000, `Stylized Rendering Techniques for Scalable Real-Time 3D Animation`: silhouettes, material/mesh boundaries and crease edges are primary cartoon rendering structures.
- Gooch, Reinhard & Gooch, ACM TOG 2004, `Human Facial Illustrations`: abstract facial illustrations preserve recognition effectiveness while removing photographic detail.
- Winnemöller, Olsen & Gooch, SIGGRAPH 2006, `Real-Time Video Abstraction`: suppress low-importance contrast, reinforce significant edges, soft-quantize color for cartoon-like abstraction.
- Kalnins et al., SIGGRAPH 2003, `Coherent Stylized Silhouettes`: silhouette coherence is a central animation constraint.

## GLOBAL MEMORY LAW
These two anchors and their derived laws are not temporary references. They are the default ZORR visual-production laws until explicitly superseded by OWNER authority.

Character Truth may change geometry/identity variables. It may NOT silently discard the global drawing discipline.
Material-specific identity may locally exceed texture envelopes. It may NOT turn the image into uncontrolled high-frequency noise.

STATUS = ARCHIVED / ACTIVE / RECOVERABLE
